WHAT WAS BUILT (the `grade` subcommand, tools/bakeoff.sh): `grade <run> seal-key <key-path>` records the answer key's sha256 into grade/seal.json BEFORE any grading (T447: the key must predate the outputs), never stores the key text, never overwrites an existing seal with a different key, and refuses a run with no lanes.json (G5: no dispatch record, no grading). `grade <run> anonymize` builds blind grading inputs — one <letter>.md per ok lane copied from the lane's out.sanitized.md (G4: self-identification stripped BEFORE grading; the original out.md is never touched), letters assigned by the deterministic name-hash shuffle (identical to the manual anonymize.py practice), and writes grade/lanes-map.sealed.json + grade/seal-record.json (map hash, per-artifact hashes, self-identified letters) while NEVER printing the map; refuses before the key is sealed and when already anonymized. `grade <run> submit --grader <label> --artifact <A> --scores <json> [--controls <json>]` records one grade; MECHANICAL G3 refuses (exit 2, naming G3) when model_family(grader) == model_family(lane behind the letter) — a same-family model is not a grader of that lane — and also refuses unknown letters, non-canonical grader labels, non-JSON scores, duplicates (grader, artifact), a missing/tampered key, and an un-anonymized run; accepted grades append to grade/grades.jsonl (append-only, immutable) and refusals append to grade/refusals.jsonl (the enforcement record); stdout never reveals the map. `grade <run> status` reports grading state without the map. `grade <run> unseal [--force <reason>]` is the only command that prints the map, and refuses while any artifact is ungraded (T447), when the map hash or an artifact hash no longer matches its seal (no override — a broken seal voids the round), when the key was edited, and when any recorded grade would fail G3 at the counting layer (count_grades() re-checks, belt-and-suspenders); --force records a deliberate early unseal. The seal is process-level and stated honestly: the map is plaintext JSON on disk (the dispatcher could read it), but the harness never prints it before unseal, refuses to unseal while grading is incomplete, and detects post-hoc edits; the grader model never receives the map at all.
